claim: One key bottleneck in understanding the human genome is the relative under-characterization of 90% of protein coding regions.
source: One key bottleneck in understanding the human genome is the relative under-characterization of 90% of protein coding regions.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of genomic knowledge presented in the abstract without specific experimental data or citations in this sentence.

claim: A collection of 1200 transgenic zebrafish strains was made with the gene-break transposon (GBT) protein trap.
source: We report a collection of 1200 transgenic zebrafish strains made with the gene-break transposon (GBT) protein trap to simultaneously report and reversibly knockdown the tagged genes.
evidence: This is a direct report of the experimental work performed in this study, describing the creation of the GBT collection.

claim: The GBT protein trap can simultaneously report and reversibly knockdown tagged genes.
source: We report a collection of 1200 transgenic zebrafish strains made with the gene-break transposon (GBT) protein trap to simultaneously report and reversibly knockdown the tagged genes.
evidence: This describes the functional capabilities of the GBT system as demonstrated in the study.

claim: Protein trap-associated mRFP expression shows previously undocumented expression of 35% of cloned genes at 2 days post-fertilization.
source: Protein trap-associated mRFP expression shows previously undocumented expression of 35% and 90% of cloned genes at 2 and 4 days post-fertilization, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study's expression analysis comparing GBT data to existing databases.

claim: Protein trap-associated mRFP expression shows previously undocumented expression of 90% of cloned genes at 4 days post-fertilization.
source: Protein trap-associated mRFP expression shows previously undocumented expression of 35% and 90% of cloned genes at 2 and 4 days post-fertilization, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study's expression analysis comparing GBT data to existing databases.

claim: Investigated GBT alleles regularly show 99% gene-specific mRNA knockdown.
source: Further, investigated alleles regularly show 99% gene-specific mRNA knockdown.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement of knockdown efficiency from qRT-PCR experiments.

claim: Homozygous GBT animals in ryr1b phenocopied established mutants.
source: Homozygous GBT animals in ryr1b, fras1, tnnt2a, edar and hmcn1 phenocopied established mutants.
evidence: This is a direct observation from phenotypic analysis comparing GBT lines to known mutants.

claim: Homozygous GBT animals in fras1 phenocopied established mutants.
source: Homozygous GBT animals in ryr1b, fras1, tnnt2a, edar and hmcn1 phenocopied established mutants.
evidence: This is a direct observation from phenotypic analysis comparing GBT lines to known mutants.

claim: Homozygous GBT animals in tnnt2a phenocopied established mutants.
source: Homozygous GBT animals in ryr1b, fras1, tnnt2a, edar and hmcn1 phenocopied established mutants.
evidence: This is a direct observation from phenotypic analysis comparing GBT lines to known mutants.

claim: Homozygous GBT animals in edar phenocopied established mutants.
source: Homozygous GBT animals in ryr1b, fras1, tnnt2a, edar and hmcn1 phenocopied established mutants.
evidence: This is a direct observation from phenotypic analysis comparing GBT lines to known mutants.

claim: Homozygous GBT animals in hmcn1 phenocopied established mutants.
source: Homozygous GBT animals in ryr1b, fras1, tnnt2a, edar and hmcn1 phenocopied established mutants.
evidence: This is a direct observation from phenotypic analysis comparing GBT lines to known mutants.

claim: 204 cloned lines trapped diverse proteins.
source: 204 cloned lines trapped diverse proteins, including 64 orthologs of human disease-associated genes with 40 as potential new disease models.
evidence: This is a summary of the molecular cloning and annotation results from the study.

claim: 64 cloned lines are orthologs of human disease-associated genes.
source: 204 cloned lines trapped diverse proteins, including 64 orthologs of human disease-associated genes with 40 as potential new disease models.
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis comparing trapped genes to human disease databases.

claim: 40 GBT lines represent potential new disease models.
source: 204 cloned lines trapped diverse proteins, including 64 orthologs of human disease-associated genes with 40 as potential new disease models.
evidence: This is based on database searches showing no existing models for these disease-associated genes.

claim: GBT ryr1b homozygous animals show severely reduced skeletal muscle Ca2+ transients.
source: Severely reduced skeletal muscle Ca2+ transients in GBT ryr1b homozygous animals validated the ability to explore molecular mechanisms of genetic diseases.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from calcium imaging experiments comparing wildtype and mutant animals.

claim: Analyses of genomic sequences from over 100 vertebrate species have revealed that we need more than nucleic acid sequence alone to comprehend the vertebrate genome.
source: Analyses of genomic sequences from over 100 vertebrate species (Meadows and Lindblad-Toh, 2017) have revealed that we need more than nucleic acid sequence alone to comprehend the vertebrate genome.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Meadows and Lindblad-Toh, 2017.

claim: A more complete understanding of any genetic locus requires knowledge of its expression pattern and its function(s) in subcellular, cellular, and organismal contexts.
source: A more complete understanding of any genetic locus requires knowledge of its expression pattern and its function(s) in subcellular, cellular, and organismal contexts—the compendium of information that can be described as a gene 'codex'.
evidence: This is a conceptual statement about what constitutes comprehensive gene annotation.

claim: The expression patterns and functions of most protein coding genes remain surprisingly uncharacterized.
source: Despite their importance, the expression patterns and functions of most protein coding genes remain surprisingly uncharacterized.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of genomic knowledge.

claim: The number of genes linked to human disease without functional insights into their gene-disease relationships highlights the significance of this knowledge gap.
source: The number of these genes linked to human disease without functional insights into their gene-disease relationships highlights the significance of this knowledge gap (Kettleborough et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Kettleborough et al., 2013.

claim: 80% of rare, undiagnosed diseases are thought to have genetic underpinnings.
source: In recent estimates, 80% of rare, undiagnosed diseases are thought to have genetic underpinnings (Robe, 2005; Varga et al., 2018; Wangler et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations (Robe, 2005; Varga et al., 2018; Wangler et al., 2017).

claim: Zebrafish has emerged as an outstanding model to bridge the gap between sequence and function in the vertebrate genome.
source: Zebrafish (Danio rerio) has emerged as an outstanding model to bridge the gap between sequence and function in the vertebrate genome.
evidence: This is a general statement about the utility of zebrafish as a model organism.

claim: Investigations of gene function in zebrafish are amenable to both forward and reverse genetic approaches.
source: Investigations of gene function in zebrafish, from organismal to subcellular, are amenable to both forward and reverse genetic approaches (Stoeger et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Stoeger et al., 2018.

claim: The natural transparency of developing zebrafish enables live, non-invasive collection of gene expression data at a subcellular resolution on an organismal scale.
source: Additionally, the natural transparency of developing zebrafish enables live, non-invasive collection of gene expression data at a subcellular resolution on an organismal scale.
evidence: This is a well-established characteristic of zebrafish as a model organism.

claim: The gene-break transposon (GBT) was previously developed as a unique, revertible mutagenesis tool with elements that cooperate to report gene sequence, expression pattern, and function.
source: To begin constructing this vertebrate codex, we previously developed a unique, revertible mutagenesis tool called the gene-break transposon (GBT) with elements that cooperate to report gene sequence, expression pattern, and function (Clark et al., 2011a).
evidence: This refers to previously published work cited as Clark et al., 2011a.

claim: When integrated in the sense orientation of a transcriptional unit, the GBT protein trap overrides endogenous splicing and creates a fusion between upstream exons and its start-codon deficient monomeric RFP (mRFP) reporter.
source: Specifically, when integrated in the sense orientation of a transcriptional unit, the GBT protein trap overrides endogenous splicing and creates a fusion between upstream exons and its start-codon deficient monomeric RFP (mRFP) reporter.
evidence: This describes the molecular mechanism of the GBT system.

claim: The strong internal polyadenylation site and putative border element following the mRFP truncate the gene product.
source: Then, the strong internal polyadenylation site and putative border element following the mRFP truncate the gene product.
evidence: This describes a functional element of the GBT construct design.

claim: The GBT construct is flanked by loxP sites on either side to enable excision and subsequent rescue with Cre-recombinase.
source: Finally, the GBT construct is flanked by loxP sites on either side to enable excision and subsequent rescue with Cre-recombinase (Clark et al., 2011a).
evidence: This describes a design feature of the GBT system supported by citation to Clark et al., 2011a.

claim: Visualization of the start-codon deficient mRFP reporter requires an in-frame integration.
source: Visualization of the start-codon deficient mRFP reporter requires an in-frame integration.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of the molecular design of the reporter.

claim: In the original GBT protein trap construct RP2.1, the in-frame requirement restricts mRFP expression to a single reading frame.
source: In the original GBT protein trap construct, RP2.1 (Figure 1A), this in-frame requirement restricts mRFP expression to a single reading frame and leaves the potential to truncate genes without reporting their expression with mRFP (Clark et al., 2011a).
evidence: This describes a limitation of the original RP2.1 construct as reported in Clark et al., 2011a.

claim: The original RP2.1 construct leaves the potential to truncate genes without reporting their expression with mRFP.
source: In the original GBT protein trap construct, RP2.1 (Figure 1A), this in-frame requirement restricts mRFP expression to a single reading frame and leaves the potential to truncate genes without reporting their expression with mRFP (Clark et al., 2011a).
evidence: This describes a limitation of the original RP2.1 construct as reported in Clark et al., 2011a.

claim: A new series of GBT protein trap constructs was developed, including versions to trap expression in each of the three potential reading frames.
source: We therefore developed a new series of GBT protein trap constructs, including versions to trap expression in each of the three potential reading frames (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes new constructs developed in this study, shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Over 800 additional GBT protein trap lines with visible mRFP expression at 2 days post-fertilization or four dpf were generated using the new vectors.
source: Alongside the original, we employed these new vectors in zebrafish to generate and catalog over 800 additional GBT protein trap lines with visible mRFP expression at 2 days post-fertilization (dpf) (end of embryogenesis) or four dpf (larval stage).
evidence: This is a direct report of the experimental work performed in this study.

claim: 147 of the additional GBT lines were cloned and candidate genes were identified.
source: 147 of these additional GBT lines were cloned, and candidate genes were identified for another 144 GBT lines.
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of the molecular cloning work performed.

claim: Candidate genes were identified for another 144 GBT lines.
source: 147 of these additional GBT lines were cloned, and candidate genes were identified for another 144 GBT lines.
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of the molecular cloning work performed.

claim: mRFP expression in cloned GBT lines showcased novel expression patterns for a population of genes encoding diverse proteins in function and localization.
source: mRFP expression in cloned GBT lines showcased novel expression patterns for a population of genes encoding diverse proteins in function and localization, including 64 implicated in human disease.
evidence: This is based on imaging and bioinformatic analysis of the GBT lines.

claim: Animals homozygous for the GBT allele in ryr1b displayed severely dampened skeletal muscle Ca2+ transients.
source: Further, animals homozygous for the GBT allele in ryr1b displayed severely dampened skeletal muscle Ca2+ transients, demonstrating the ability to elucidate molecular mechanisms of genetic disorders.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from calcium imaging experiments.

claim: The RP2 series incorporates a protein-trap cassette fused with three reading frames of AUG-less mRFP reporter and a 3' exon trap cassette with GFP reporter.
source: RP2 and RP8 incorporate a protein-trap cassette fused with three reading frames of AUG-less mRFP reporter and a 3' exon trap cassette with GFP or tagBFP reporters, respectively.
evidence: This describes the design of the RP2 constructs shown in Figure 1.

claim: The RP8 series incorporates a protein-trap cassette fused with three reading frames of AUG-less mRFP reporter and a 3' exon trap cassette with tagBFP reporter.
source: RP2 and RP8 incorporate a protein-trap cassette fused with three reading frames of AUG-less mRFP reporter and a 3' exon trap cassette with GFP or tagBFP reporters, respectively.
evidence: This describes the design of the RP8 constructs shown in Figure 1.

claim: All RP2 and RP8 series constructs readily produced mRFP fusion proteins expressed from their endogenous promoters.
source: Using all five of these new GBT constructs in zebrafish, we conducted an initial screen for expression of protein trap mRFP and observed that all RP2 and RP8 series constructs readily produced mRFP fusion proteins expressed from their endogenous promoters (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on direct observation of mRFP expression in zebrafish, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Over 1,200 GBT lines with robust mRFP expression in heterozygous F2 animals at two dpf and/or four dpf have been cataloged.
source: To date, we have now cataloged over 1,200 GBT lines with robust mRFP expression in heterozygous F2 animals at two dpf and/or four dpf according to our screening pipeline and made all imaging data freely accessible on zfishbook (www.zfishbook.org) (Clark et al., 2012; Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct report of the screening and cataloging work, with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: All imaging data for the GBT lines have been made freely accessible on zfishbook.
source: To date, we have now cataloged over 1,200 GBT lines with robust mRFP expression in heterozygous F2 animals at two dpf and/or four dpf according to our screening pipeline and made all imaging data freely accessible on zfishbook (www.zfishbook.org) (Clark et al., 2012; Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the data sharing approach for the study.

claim: The 1,200 GBT lines have been cryopreserved and retained at the Mayo Clinic Zebrafish Facility (MCZF) with a copy also sent to the Zebrafish International Resource Center (ZIRC).
source: We have cryopreserved these 1,200 GBT lines and have retained them at the Mayo Clinic Zebrafish Facility (MCZF) with a copy also sent to the Zebrafish International Resource Center (ZIRC) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the preservation and distribution of the biological resources.

claim: Traditional molecular methods such as inverse PCR and TAIL PCR are labor-intensive and represent a functional bottleneck in identifying randomly integrated loci in GBT lines.
source: Traditional molecular methods, such as inverse PCR (iPCR) and thermal asymmetric interlaced (TAIL) PCR and 5' and 3' rapid amplification of cDNA ends (RACE), are labor-intensive and represent a functional bottleneck in identifying randomly integrated loci in GBT lines.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of traditional molecular cloning methods.

claim: A rapid cloning process based on massive parallel sequencing technology of the Illumina MiSeq was employed to overcome the bottleneck in identifying integrated loci.
source: To overcome this, we employed a rapid cloning process based on methods used to isolate retroviral integrations that leverage the massive parallel sequencing technology of the Illumina MiSeq and a custom bioinformatics pipeline that involves both mapping and annotation (Figure 2B; Varshney et al., 2013a; Varshney et al., 2013b).
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study, supported by citations to Varshney et al., 2013a and 2013b.

claim: 204 GBT-candidate lines met the highest stringency of confirmed expression linkage and were classified as 'GBT-confirmed lines'.
source: At the end of this pipeline, 204 GBT-candidate lines met the highest stringency of confirmed expression linkage and were classified as 'GBT-confirmed lines' (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the molecular validation pipeline.

claim: 57 of the GBT-confirmed lines have been previously published.
source: While 57 of these GBT-confirmed lines have been previously published (Clark et al., 2011a; Ding et al., 2013; Ding et al., 2017; El-Rass et al., 2017; Ma et al., 2020; Westcot et al., 2015), 147 of these GBT-confirmed lines are newly characterized in this manuscript and were selected for confirmation based upon their expression pattern and/or homozygous phenotype (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous publications.

claim: 147 GBT-confirmed lines are newly characterized in this manuscript.
source: While 57 of these GBT-confirmed lines have been previously published (Clark et al., 2011a; Ding et al., 2013; Ding et al., 2017; El-Rass et al., 2017; Ma et al., 2020; Westcot et al., 2015), 147 of these GBT-confirmed lines are newly characterized in this manuscript and were selected for confirmation based upon their expression pattern and/or homozygous phenotype (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the novel contributions of this study.

claim: A small subset of GBT-confirmed lines mapped to areas in the genome without annotated transcripts.
source: A small subset of these GBT-confirmed lines mapped to areas in the genome without annotated transcripts.
evidence: This is based on mapping the integration sites to the reference genome.

claim: Publicly available RNA-sequencing data revealed reads flanking a majority of the mapped integrations in unannotated regions.
source: Publicly available RNA-sequencing data (White et al., 2017) revealed reads flanking a majority of these mapped integrations.
evidence: This is based on analysis of public RNA-seq data cited as White et al., 2017.

claim: Some RNA-seq reads contained evidence of splicing in the sense orientation of the mRFP reporter.
source: Some of these reads contained evidence of splicing in the sense orientation of the mRFP reporter (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: Another 144 GBT-candidate lines from the sequencing pipeline have yet to be confirmed.
source: Finally, another 144 GBT-candidate lines from this pipeline have yet to be confirmed (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the current status of the molecular validation work.

claim: qRT-PCR data for all 26 RP2.1-derived GBT-confirmed lines tested showed at minimum 97% knockdown in animals homozygous for the RP2.1 alleles.
source: We therefore compiled qRT-PCR data to compare wild-type and truncated, mRFP-fused transcript levels for all 26 RP2.1-derived GBT-confirmed lines that we and others have tested (Clark et al., 2011a; Ding et al., 2013; Ding et al., 2017, GBT0235—this manuscript). This compilation determined at minimum 97% knockdown in animals homozygous for the RP2.1 alleles.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from qRT-PCR experiments across multiple studies.

claim: The FlipTrap system produced a range of 70–96% knockdown in six tested fish alleles.
source: The FlipTrap system produced a range of 70–96% knockdown in six tested fish alleles (Trinh et al., 2011), similar to our initial R-series protein trap vectors (R14-R15) that contained a single splice acceptor and a simple transcriptional terminator (Liao et al., 2012; Petzold et al., 2009).
evidence: This is based on data from Trinh et al., 2011, comparing different protein trap systems.

claim: The initial R-series protein trap vectors (R14-R15) produced knockdown similar to the FlipTrap system.
source: The FlipTrap system produced a range of 70–96% knockdown in six tested fish alleles (Trinh et al., 2011), similar to our initial R-series protein trap vectors (R14-R15) that contained a single splice acceptor and a simple transcriptional terminator (Liao et al., 2012; Petzold et al., 2009).
evidence: This is based on data from Liao et al., 2012 and Petzold et al., 2009.

claim: The pFT1 system produced 89–94% knockdown from four tested fish alleles.
source: The pFT1, which contains a single splice acceptor, but a tandem array of five simple polyadenylation sites, appears to be an improvement over these systems with 89–94% knockdown from four tested fish alleles (Ni et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on data from Ni et al., 2012.

claim: The 97% minimum knockdown observed with RP2.1 is quantitatively higher than other protein trap systems.
source: The 97% minimum knockdown observed with RP2.1 is quantitatively higher than these other systems and could be deployed with other insertional genome engineering approaches.
evidence: This is a comparative analysis of knockdown efficiency data across different systems.

claim: In 179 mRFP+ GBT lines, 12 recessive phenotypes visible during the first five days of development were identified.
source: In 179 mRFP+ GBT lines, we identified 12 recessive phenotypes visible during the first five days of development that, among others, included lethal, cardiac, muscular, and integumentary defects as reported in previous studies (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the phenotypic screening.

claim: The identified recessive phenotypes included lethal, cardiac, muscular, and integumentary defects.
source: In 179 mRFP+ GBT lines, we identified 12 recessive phenotypes visible during the first five days of development that, among others, included lethal, cardiac, muscular, and integumentary defects as reported in previous studies (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This describes the types of phenotypes observed in the screen.

claim: A subset of the identified phenotypes stem from GBT integrations in genes with established loss of function mutant phenotypes including ryr1b, tnnt2a, fras1, hmcn1, and edar.
source: Molecular analyses revealed that a subset of these phenotypes stem from GBT integrations in genes with established loss of function mutant phenotypes including ryr1b, tnnt2a, fras1, hmcn1, and edar (Clark et al., 2011a; Westcot et al., 2015; Hatzold J et al., unpublished).
evidence: This is based on molecular cloning and comparison to known mutants, supported by citations.

claim: Five GBT-confirmed lines (ryr1b, tnnt2a, fras1, hmcn1, and edar) phenocopied their respective homozygous mutants generated with other strategies.
source: In accord with their mRNA knockdown potency, these five GBT-confirmed lines (ryr1b, tnnt2a, fras1, hmcn1, and edar) phenocopied their respective homozygous mutants generated with other strategies and thereby validated the mutagenicity of the GBT constructs.
evidence: This is based on phenotypic comparison between GBT lines and established mutants.

claim: 17 GBT-confirmed lines have been published with homozygous phenotypes ranging from embryonic lethal, to reduced adult viability, to differences in pharmacological susceptibility.
source: To date, 17 of our GBT-confirmed lines have been published with homozygous phenotypes ranging from embryonic lethal, to reduced adult viability, to differences in pharmacological susceptibility (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a summary of published phenotypic data from GBT lines.

claim: A GBT line with skeletal muscle-specific mRFP expression and a slow swimming phenotype was identified during the initial GBT library creation.
source: During the initial GBT library creation, we identified a GBT line with skeletal muscle-specific mRFP expression and a slow swimming phenotype (Clark et al., 2011a).
evidence: This refers to previously published work cited as Clark et al., 2011a.

claim: The skeletal muscle-specific GBT line possesses an RP2.1 integration between exon 81 and exon 82 of ryr1b.
source: We confirmed that this line possesses an RP2.1 integration between exon 81 and exon 82 of ryr1b and designated it ryr1bmn0348Gt.
evidence: This is based on molecular cloning of the integration site.

claim: Animals homozygous for the ryr1bmn0348Gt allele show 97% knockdown of wild-type ryr1b mRNA levels.
source: Animals homozygous for this ryr1bmn0348Gt allele show 97% knockdown of wild-type ryr1b mRNA levels (Clark et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data from Clark et al., 2011a.

claim: ryr1b orthologs are known across species to encode calcium-activated calcium channels that release sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ stores to facilitate excitation-contraction coupling in skeletal muscles.
source: ryr1b orthologs are known across species to encode calcium-activated calcium channels that release sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ stores to facilitate excitation-contraction coupling in skeletal muscles (Hernández-Ochoa et al., 2015; Hirata et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ryr1b function supported by citations.

claim: PTZ-treated ryr1b+/+ and ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals showed spontaneous, convulsion-associated Ca2+ transients in their myocytes at two dpf.
source: Likewise, PTZ-treated ryr1b+/+ and ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals showed spontaneous, convulsion-associated Ca2+ transients in their myocytes at two dpf (Figures 4C–E,G–I).
evidence: This is a direct observation from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: PTZ-induced Ca2+ transients in myocytes of ryr1b+/+ animals had higher peak amplitude when averaged within fish than those in ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
source: However, PTZ-induced Ca2+ transients in myocytes of ryr1b+/+ animals had higher peak amplitude when averaged within fish (Figure 4J–K) or within myocytes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and shorter rise time (Figure 4J,M) than those in ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: PTZ-induced Ca2+ transients in myocytes of ryr1b+/+ animals had higher peak amplitude when averaged within myocytes than those in ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
source: However, PTZ-induced Ca2+ transients in myocytes of ryr1b+/+ animals had higher peak amplitude when averaged within fish (Figure 4J–K) or within myocytes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and shorter rise time (Figure 4J,M) than those in ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: PTZ-induced Ca2+ transients in myocytes of ryr1b+/+ animals had shorter rise time than those in ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
source: However, PTZ-induced Ca2+ transients in myocytes of ryr1b+/+ animals had higher peak amplitude when averaged within fish (Figure 4J–K) or within myocytes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and shorter rise time (Figure 4J,M) than those in ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: PTZ-induced Ca2+ transient peak-width was not significantly different between ryr1b+/+ and ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
source: PTZ-induced Ca2+ transient peak-width (Figure 4J,L) and decay time (Figure 4J,N) were not significantly different between ryr1b+/+ and ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
evidence: This is a statistical result from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: PTZ-induced Ca2+ transient decay time was not significantly different between ryr1b+/+ and ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
source: PTZ-induced Ca2+ transient peak-width (Figure 4J,L) and decay time (Figure 4J,N) were not significantly different between ryr1b+/+ and ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
evidence: This is a statistical result from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Myocytes in ryr1b+/+ animals had more Ca2+ transients during the imaging period than myocytes in ryr1bRP2.1/RP2.1 animals.
source: In contrast, myocytes in ryr1b+/+ animals had more Ca2+ transients during the imaging period than myocytes in ryr1bRP2.1/RP2.1 animals (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A smaller peak amplitude, slower upstroke, and lower frequency of Ca2+ transients in skeletal muscle likely provide the basis for the slow swimming phenotype in ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
source: We were thus able to use a GBT-confirmed line to demonstrate that a smaller peak amplitude (consistent with relatively relaxed [Hirata et al., 2007]), slower upstroke, and lower frequency of Ca2+ transients in skeletal muscle likely provide the basis for the slow swimming phenotype in ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
evidence: This is an inference based on the calcium imaging data and comparison to known mutants.

claim: The consistency of findings in ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt with those in relatively relaxed mutants validates the functional genome annotation available with the GBT mutagenic system.
source: The consistency of our findings in ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt with those in relatively relaxed mutants (Hirata et al., 2007) validates the functional genome annotation available with the GBT mutagenic system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the GBT line phenotype to published mutants.

claim: 82% of OMIM listed human disease-associated genes can be related to at least one zebrafish ortholog.
source: Intriguingly, 82% of OMIM listed human disease-associated genes (2601 genes) can be related to at least one zebrafish ortholog (Howe et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis cited as Howe et al., 2013.

claim: Within the set of GBT-confirmed lines that match a human ortholog (n = 177), 64 (36%) are integrated in genes associated with human diseases.
source: Within the set of GBT-confirmed lines that match a human ortholog (n = 177), 64 (36%) are integrated in genes associated with human diseases, including those of the nervous, circulatory, endocrine, metabolic, digestive, musculoskeletal, immune, and integumentary systems (select genes listed in Figure 5A, all 64 genes with disease-associated human orthologs listed in Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from bioinformatic analysis of the GBT-confirmed lines.

claim: The 64 human disease-associated GBT-confirmed lines include genes associated with diseases of the nervous, circulatory, endocrine, metabolic, digestive, musculoskeletal, immune, and integumentary systems.
source: Within the set of GBT-confirmed lines that match a human ortholog (n = 177), 64 (36%) are integrated in genes associated with human diseases, including those of the nervous, circulatory, endocrine, metabolic, digestive, musculoskeletal, immune, and integumentary systems (select genes listed in Figure 5A, all 64 genes with disease-associated human orthologs listed in Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This describes the diversity of disease systems represented in the GBT collection.

claim: 40 of the human disease-associated GBT-confirmed lines represent potential novel genetic disease models as no established disease models in mice or zebrafish were found for orthologs of these genes.
source: 40 of these human disease-associated GBT-confirmed lines represent potential novel genetic disease models as we failed to find a description for any established disease models in mice or zebrafish for orthologs of these genes (Figure 5B and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is based on database searches for existing models.

claim: Imaging of GBT-confirmed lines has revealed diverse cellular and subcellular protein expression patterns.
source: We and others have previously used imaging to investigate effective protein trapping in GBT-confirmed lines. This imaging has revealed diverse cellular and subcellular protein expression patterns (Clark et al., 2011a; Ding et al., 2013; Ding et al., 2017; El-Rass et al., 2017; Liao et al., 2012; Petzold et al., 2009; Westcot et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous imaging studies.

claim: Multi-area tiling with a 20× objective on a Lightsheet microscope enabled rapid acquisition of 3-dimensional mRFP fusion protein localization across the entire organism.
source: Multi-area tiling with a 20 × objective enabled rapid acquisition of 3-dimensional mRFP fusion protein localization across the entire organism (Figure 6A).
evidence: This describes the imaging methodology used in this study.

claim: Confocal imaging in areas of interest revealed subcellular resolution detail.
source: Confocal imaging in areas of interest revealed even more detail with subcellular resolution (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: This describes the imaging methodology and results shown in Figure 6.

claim: Confocal imaging demonstrated diverse subcellular localizations in GBT-confirmed lines, GBT-candidate lines, and GBT lines.
source: Further confocal imaging demonstrated diverse subcellular localizations in GBT-confirmed lines, (Figure 6B–C) GBT-candidate lines, and GBT lines (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on confocal imaging data shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: 177 of the GBT-trapped genes were annotated to their human orthologs in at least one public database.
source: 177 of the GBT-trapped genes were annotated to their human orthologs in at least one public database (ZFIN, Ensembl, Homologene, and InParanoid version 8) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis using multiple databases.

claim: PANTHER protein classification revealed that 105 human orthologs (60%, n = 176) are classified to at least one of 21 protein classes.
source: PANTHER protein classification revealed that 105 human orthologs (60%, n = 176: see Materials and methods) are classified to at least one of 21 protein classes, and 19 human orthologs (11%) belong to transcription factors (Figure 6D and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on PANTHER database analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: 19 human orthologs (11%) of GBT-trapped genes belong to transcription factors.
source: PANTHER protein classification revealed that 105 human orthologs (60%, n = 176: see Materials and methods) are classified to at least one of 21 protein classes, and 19 human orthologs (11%) belong to transcription factors (Figure 6D and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on PANTHER database analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Human Protein Atlas and UniProtKB subcellular localization data showed diverse classifications of expression with a large group of nuclear localized human orthologs of the 177 GBT-confirmed loci.
source: Human Protein Atlas and UniProtKB subcellular localization data likewise showed diverse classifications of expression with a large group of nuclear localized human orthologs of these 177 GBT-confirmed loci (Figure 6E and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is based on database analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: LRPPRC (human ortholog of lrpprc (GBT0235)) was not annotated to a protein class in PANTHER but mapped to mitochondria in Human Protein Atlas.
source: We found that LRPPRC (human ortholog of lrpprc (GBT0235)—Figure 6A–B) was not annotated to a protein class in PANTHER but mapped to mitochondria in Human Protein Atlas, consistent with its puncta expression pattern (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: This is based on database analysis and comparison to imaging data in Figure 6A-B.

claim: RYR1 (human ortholog of ryr1b (GBT0348)) was annotated as a transporter in PANTHER and was mapped to the cytosol, Golgi apparatus, and vesicles in Human Protein Atlas.
source: RYR1 (human ortholog of ryr1b (GBT0348)—Figure 6C) was annotated as a transporter in PANTHER and was mapped to the cytosol, Golgi apparatus, and vesicles in Human Protein Atlas, consistent with its more uniform expression pattern (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is based on database analysis and comparison to imaging data in Figure 6C.

claim: Protein class ontology and known subcellular localizations of cloned GBT genes suggest that the GBT system traps and enables functional annotation for a rich diversity of proteins.
source: Overall, protein class ontology and known subcellular localizations of cloned GBT genes suggest that the GBT system traps and enables functional annotation for a rich diversity of proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the bioinformatic and imaging analyses.

claim: GBT-confirmed lines in orthologs of human genes without a known subcellular localization potentiate the discovery of their subcellular expression pattern in the context of a living animal.
source: Additionally, the GBT-confirmed lines in orthologs of human genes without a known subcellular localization potentiate the discovery of their subcellular expression pattern in the context of a living animal.
evidence: This is an inference about the potential utility of GBT lines for novel discoveries.

claim: GBT-confirmed lines exhibited expression patterns that are tissue specific and include assorted brain regions, heart, skin, muscle, vasculature, and blood.
source: Importantly, these GBT-confirmed lines exhibited expression patterns that are tissue specific and include assorted brain regions, heart, skin, muscle, vasculature, and blood (Figure 7A–R).
evidence: This is based on imaging data shown in Figure 7A-R.

claim: GBT-confirmed lines revealed expression patterns for 67 genes at 2 dpf without publicly available expression data in ZFIN.
source: Our GBT-confirmed lines revealed expression patterns (available on www.zfishbook.org) for 67 genes at 2 dpf and 174 genes at four dpf without publicly available expression data in ZFIN (Figure 7S–T).
evidence: This is based on comparison of GBT imaging data to the ZFIN database, shown in Figure 7S.

claim: GBT-confirmed lines revealed expression patterns for 174 genes at four dpf without publicly available expression data in ZFIN.
source: Our GBT-confirmed lines revealed expression patterns (available on www.zfishbook.org) for 67 genes at 2 dpf and 174 genes at four dpf without publicly available expression data in ZFIN (Figure 7S–T).
evidence: This is based on comparison of GBT imaging data to the ZFIN database, shown in Figure 7T.

claim: GBT technology represents the first method for revertible allele generation in vertebrates outside of the mouse model.
source: GBT technology represents the first method for revertible allele generation in vertebrates outside of the mouse model (Clark et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the GBT system supported by citation to Clark et al., 2011a.

claim: The RP2 series potentiates in-frame mRFP for any intron with Tol2-mediated integration.
source: While each individual construct still only integrates in-frame in a subset of introns, the RP2 series potentiates in-frame mRFP for any intron with Tol2-mediated integration.
evidence: This is an inference about the capabilities of the RP2 series based on its design.

claim: All RP8 constructs include new restriction enzyme sites that render them modular for custom engineering.
source: All RP8 constructs include new restriction enzyme sites that render them modular for custom engineering.
evidence: This describes a design feature of the RP8 constructs.

claim: RP8 series constructs use a smaller backbone designed to enhance transgenic efficiency.
source: Additionally, RP8 series constructs use a smaller backbone designed to enhance transgenic efficiency.
evidence: This describes a design feature of the RP8 constructs.

claim: The lens-specific tagBFP in RP8 was found to be equally useful in screening founders with GBT integrations.
source: We found this lens-specific tagBFP to be equally useful in screening founders with GBT integrations.
evidence: This is based on practical experience using the RP8 constructs in screening.

claim: The knockdown between RP8 and RP2 is expected to be similar.
source: While we did not explicitly validate that the RP8 series provides transcriptional effects equivalent to the RP2 series, the major functional change in RP8 lies in its 3' exon trap. We therefore expect the knockdown to be similar between RP8 and RP2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity of the 5' protein trap design between RP8 and RP2.

claim: The FlipTrap system is mutagenic in the presence of Cre-recombinase.
source: Dr. Fraser's group developed the FlipTrap system (Trinh et al., 2011) that is mutagenic in the presence of Cre-recombinase.
evidence: This is based on the citation to Trinh et al., 2011.

claim: The FlipTrap system is primarily focused on imaging fusion proteins in vivo and addressing cellular dynamics.
source: However, this FlipTrap system is primarily focused on imaging fusion proteins in vivo and addressing cellular dynamics.
evidence: This is a characterization of the FlipTrap system based on its published applications.

claim: The FT1 system uses either Cre or Flp recombinase to regulate its alleles depending on the original insertion orientation.
source: The Chen lab developed a complementary flipping system called the FT1 system that uses either Cre or Flp recombinase to regulate its alleles depending on the original insertion orientation (Ni et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on the citation to Ni et al., 2012.

claim: The 5' protein trap in the GBT system is terminated through an enhanced polyadenylation signal in conjunction with a putative border element.
source: The 5' protein trap in the GBT system is terminated through an enhanced polyadenylation signal in conjunction with a putative border element and a second splice acceptor in the 3' exon trap helps eliminate any pass-through.
evidence: This describes the molecular design of the GBT system.

claim: A second splice acceptor in the 3' exon trap helps eliminate any pass-through.
source: The 5' protein trap in the GBT system is terminated through an enhanced polyadenylation signal in conjunction with a putative border element and a second splice acceptor in the 3' exon trap helps eliminate any pass-through.
evidence: This describes the molecular design of the GBT system.

claim: The GBT system possesses a 3' exon trap that serves as a means for screening integrations, reports 3' sequence, and possesses the ability to trap non-coding RNAs that undergo splicing.
source: In addition to a 5' protein trap, our GBT system also possesses a 3' exon trap that serves as a means for screening integrations, reports 3' sequence, and possesses the ability to trap (without mRFP expression) non-coding RNAs that undergo splicing (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the functional capabilities of the 3' exon trap in the GBT system.

claim: The mutagenic efficacy of the GBT system is functionally similar to other genome-wide forward genetic approaches at identifying critical early developmental loci.
source: Consistent with its mRNA knockdown abilities, the mutagenic efficacy of the GBT system is functionally similar to other genome-wide forward genetic approaches at identifying critical early developmental loci.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about the GBT system's performance.

claim: The GBT system achieved 7% recovery of visible early (through five dpf) developmental phenotypes during an initial forward genetic screen.
source: The GBT system achieved 7% recovery of visible early (through five dpf) developmental phenotypes during an initial forward genetic screen.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the phenotypic screening.

claim: The 7% phenotype recovery is comparable to the 5% recovered visible phenotypes from the Sanger TILLING consortium analysis of truncated zebrafish genes.
source: This recovery is comparable to the 5% recovered visible phenotypes from the Sanger TILLING consortium analysis of truncated zebrafish genes (Kettleborough et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a comparison to published data cited as Kettleborough et al., 2013.

claim: The 7% phenotype recovery is comparable to prior retroviral and ENU zebrafish mutagenesis works that estimated between 1400 and 2400 genes (~5–9% of the genome) would result in a visible embryonic phenotype when mutated.
source: Our 7% phenotype recovery is also comparable to prior retroviral (Amsterdam and Hopkins, 2004) and ENU (Haffter et al., 1996) zebrafish mutagenesis works that estimated between 1400 and 2400 genes (~5–9% of the genome) would result in a visible embryonic phenotype when mutated.
evidence: This is a comparison to published data cited as Amsterdam and Hopkins, 2004 and Haffter et al., 1996.

claim: The ryr1b GBT-confirmed line was ideal to validate the functional genome annotation abilities of GBT constructs due to the well-characterized nature of ryr1b from the relatively relaxed mutant.
source: Due to the well-characterized nature of ryr1b from the relatively relaxed mutant (Hirata et al., 2007), this line was ideal for a proof of concept experiment in this study to validate functional genome annotation with GBT constructs.
evidence: This explains the rationale for choosing ryr1b for validation experiments.

claim: Mutations in RYR1 are well-associated with a rare genetic neuromuscular disorder called central core disease.
source: For instance, mutations in RYR1, the human ortholog of ryr1b, are well-associated with a rare genetic neuromuscular disorder called central core disease.
evidence: This is established knowledge about RYR1 and human disease.

claim: Central core disease commonly presents with mild to severe muscle weakness.
source: Central core disease commonly presents with mild to severe muscle weakness (Jungbluth et al., 2018) which is analogous to the slow swimming phenotype we saw in our ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals (Clark et al., 2011a) and likely arises from similar disruptions to skeletal muscle Ca2+ transients (Figure 4).
evidence: This is based on the citation to Jungbluth et al., 2018.

claim: The muscle weakness in central core disease is analogous to the slow swimming phenotype in ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
source: Central core disease commonly presents with mild to severe muscle weakness (Jungbluth et al., 2018) which is analogous to the slow swimming phenotype we saw in our ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals (Clark et al., 2011a) and likely arises from similar disruptions to skeletal muscle Ca2+ transients (Figure 4).
evidence: This is an inference connecting the human disease phenotype to the zebrafish phenotype.

claim: The muscle weakness in central core disease likely arises from similar disruptions to skeletal muscle Ca2+ transients as seen in ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals.
source: Central core disease commonly presents with mild to severe muscle weakness (Jungbluth et al., 2018) which is analogous to the slow swimming phenotype we saw in our ryr1bmn0348Gt/mn0348Gt animals (Clark et al., 2011a) and likely arises from similar disruptions to skeletal muscle Ca2+ transients (Figure 4).
evidence: This is an inference based on the calcium imaging data in Figure 4.

claim: GBT-based mRFP-reporters demonstrate how much we still have left to understand about the expression patterns of the overall proteome.
source: Taken together, GBT-based mRFP-reporters demonstrate how much we still have left to understand about the expression patterns of the overall proteome and, ultimately, the complex codex that is our genome.
evidence: This is a general conclusion drawn from the expression data generated in the study.

claim: Nearly 40% of GBT-confirmed lines elucidated novel gene expression data at the 2-dpf stage.
source: Even at the relatively well-studied 2-dpf stage, nearly 40% of GBT-confirmed lines elucidated novel gene expression data (Figure 7).
evidence: This is based on comparison of GBT expression data to existing databases, shown in Figure 7.

claim: The remaining 144 GBT-candidate lines and over 800 GBT lines represent a rich resource for genomic discoveries.
source: The remaining 144 GBT-candidate lines and over 800 GBT lines represent a rich resource for genomic discoveries.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential utility of the unconfirmed lines.

claim: New targeted integration tools, such as GeneWeld, that employ gene editing techniques will empower labs to build custom GBT lines for their gene of interest.
source: Although our GBT lines were made with random integration, new targeted integration tools, such as GeneWeld (Wierson et al., 2020), that employ gene editing techniques will empower labs to build custom GBT lines for their gene of interest (El Khoury et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a forward-looking statement about future applications, supported by citations.

claim: The three reading frames and modularity of the RP8 series are especially well suited to targeted integration approaches.
source: The three reading frames and modularity of the RP8 series are especially well suited to targeted integration approaches.
evidence: This is an inference about the utility of the RP8 design for future applications.

claim: A combination of targeted and random integration may best facilitate discovery.
source: Further, a combination of targeted and random integration may best facilitate discovery.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future experimental strategies.

claim: GBTs are a powerful tool to investigate multigenic processes, including human disease.
source: With this approach, GBTs are a powerful tool to investigate multigenic processes, including human disease.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of the GBT system.

claim: Engineered mutant animals using CRISPR and TALEN systems frequently fail to display overt phenotypes, often explained by genetic compensation.
source: However, engineered mutant animals using approaches generate targeted indel mutation frequently fail to display overt phenotypes, often explained by genetic compensation (Balciunas, 2018; El-Brolosy and Stainier, 2017).
evidence: This is based on citations to Balciunas, 2018 and El-Brolosy and Stainier, 2017.

claim: One mechanism of genetic compensation includes cellular increases in transcripts of genes in the same family that can functionally substitute when activated in a mutant background.
source: One mechanism includes cellular increases in transcripts of genes in the same family that can functionally substitute when activated in a mutant background (Balciunas, 2018).
evidence: This is based on the citation to Balciunas, 2018.

claim: A number of studies using reverse genetics tools have revealed phenotype differences between knockouts (indel mutants) and knockdowns (antisense-treated animals) in multiple model systems.
source: Recently, a number of studies using reverse genetics tools have revealed phenotype differences between knockouts (indel mutants), and knockdowns (antisense-treated animals) in multiple model systems including Arabidopsis, Drosophila, zebrafish, mouse, and human cell lines.
evidence: This is a general statement about findings in the field.

claim: The discrepancy between knockouts and knockdowns is attributed to transcriptomic changes in mutant but not in knockdown animals.
source: This discrepancy is attributed to transcriptomic changes in mutant but not in knockdown animals (Reviewed from El-Brolosy and Stainier, 2017).
evidence: This is based on a review cited as El-Brolosy and Stainier, 2017.

claim: Knockdown of egfl7 induces severe vascular defects, whereas most egfl7 mutants exhibit no obvious defect.
source: For example, knockdown of egfl7, an endothelial extracellular matrix (ECM) gene, induces severe vascular defects, whereas most egfl7 mutants exhibit no obvious defect, resulting from upregulation of other ECM proteins, especially emilins in egfl7 mutants, but not in egfl7 morphants (Ronzitti, 2019).
evidence: This is an example from the literature cited as Ronzitti, 2019.

claim: The lack of phenotype in egfl7 mutants results from upregulation of other ECM proteins, especially emilins in egfl7 mutants, but not in egfl7 morphants.
source: For example, knockdown of egfl7, an endothelial extracellular matrix (ECM) gene, induces severe vascular defects, whereas most egfl7 mutants exhibit no obvious defect, resulting from upregulation of other ECM proteins, especially emilins in egfl7 mutants, but not in egfl7 morphants (Ronzitti, 2019).
evidence: This is an example from the literature cited as Ronzitti, 2019.

claim: mRNA processing—including nonsense-associated exon skipping and the use of alternative start or splice sites to escape nonsense-mediated decay—has been demonstrated to hinder loss-of-function approaches in zebrafish.
source: As another mechanism of genetic compensation, mRNA processing—including nonsense-associated exon skipping and the use of alternative start or splice sites to escape nonsense-mediated decay—has been recently demonstrated to hinder loss-of-function approaches in zebrafish (Anderson et al., 2017; Prykhozhij et al., 2017), in human cell lines (Lalonde et al., 2017; Winter et al., 2019) and in the human population (Jagannathan and Bradley, 2016).
evidence: This is based on multiple citations describing this mechanism.

claim: The molecular mechanism of GBT mutagenesis can normally avoid the genetic compensation effect seen with small indel mutations.
source: In contrast, the molecular mechanism of GBT mutagenesis can normally avoid this genetic compensation effect seen with small indel mutations because the strong poly (A)-trapping element in the 5' exon trap domain of RP cassettes can reduce mRNA to below 1% of the complete wild-type transcript level.
evidence: This is an inference based on the design and knockdown efficiency of the GBT system.

claim: The strong poly (A)-trapping element in the 5' exon trap domain of RP cassettes can reduce mRNA to below 1% of the complete wild-type transcript level.
source: In contrast, the molecular mechanism of GBT mutagenesis can normally avoid this genetic compensation effect seen with small indel mutations because the strong poly (A)-trapping element in the 5' exon trap domain of RP cassettes can reduce mRNA to below 1% of the complete wild-type transcript level.
evidence: This is based on the qRT-PCR data showing high knockdown efficiency.

claim: The reduction of mRNA to below 1% eliminates many sources of transcriptional adaptations triggered by a loss of function mutation, such as alternative transcriptional start sites, splicing, or alternative translation initiation.
source: This reduction eliminates many sources of transcriptional adaptations triggered by a loss of function mutation, such as alternative transcriptional start sites, splicing, or alternative translation initiation.
evidence: This is an inference about the consequences of the high knockdown efficiency.

claim: The GBT can act as a useful validation tool when targeted mutations with other technologies fail to display any phenotype.
source: The GBT can therefore act as a useful validation tool when targeted mutations with other technologies fail to display any phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of the GBT system in comparison to other methods.
